mapped_topics.label: Reduction of Quadratic form to canonical forms by Orthogonal Transformation

blocks.text: A linear transformation has the matrix form \(Y=AX\). It is non-singular when A is non-singular. An orthogonal transformation satisfies \(A^{-1}=A^T\), or \(A^TA=I\). The columns have unit length and are mutually orthogonal.
A quadratic form is homogeneous of degree two. In two variables it is \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2\); in three variables it is \(ax^2+by^2+cz^2+2hxy+2gyz+2fzx\).
The rank and determinant of the quadratic form refer to its associated symmetric matrix. A change \(X=PY\) gives \(Q=Y^TP^TAPY\). In canonical form the mixed-product terms are absent.
